headline: Amazon online store sales jump 15% with Prime Day pulled into June; grocery and essentials outgrow the rest of retail.

metrics.comp_label: Online stores sales growth (ex-FX if available)

guidance_note: Q3 2026: net sales $197-202B (+9-12%), below ~$203.9B consensus; operating income $22.5-26.5B. EPS shown is GAAP, inflated by ~$53B Anthropic-related gains.
key_messages: Online stores sales $70.4B vs $61.5B (~+15%), boosted by Prime Day moving to June 23-26 from July.
North America sales $116.2B (+16%); segment operating income $9.1B vs $7.5B, margin ~7.8%.
Third-party seller services $46.8B (+16% ex-FX); advertising $19.8B, +26%; subscriptions $13.7B, +12%.
Jassy: grocery and everyday essentials growing meaningfully faster than the rest of stores, helped by record delivery speeds.
Numerator estimated average Prime Day household spend fell to $143.45 from $156.37: more items, smaller baskets.
macro_read: Strong headline growth is partly calendar; the mix toward grocery and essentials and smaller Prime Day baskets point to a consumer who keeps spending but stays price-conscious.

sources.label: Modern Retail: groceries and essentials growing faster

notes: EPS is GAAP and includes about $53B of Anthropic-related gains, so no consensus comparison is shown.
Online stores growth is total growth, not a like-for-like comp.
